title.official: Absence of person served with notice of appointment for assessment

subdivision.heading: Assessment of Costs by Assessment Officer

operative_text.controlling:
10.40   An assessment officer may, on proof of service of the
notice of appointment and proposed bill of costs, proceed with the
assessment of costs payable despite the absence of the person
served.

BOOK_A.commentary_review_flag: Read in full, p.10-129 (lines 6971-6981): title (line 6971, 'Absence of Person Served With Notice of Appointment for Assessment'), rule text (lines 6972-6974, the footnote marker '4' after 'the absence of the person served.'), Related Provisions (lines 6976-6979, three entries wrapped across a blank line: '3.36 (failure to defend) ; 9.15(1) (b) (setting aside order on failure to appear) ; 10.16 (failure to appear on review)'), the note (lines 6980-6981, one sentence: 'This was done and upheld, especially as deference is owed to the assessment officer’s scheduling decisions.', footnote marker '5') and 2 footnotes: p.10-129 fn 4 (line 6996, history: 'Quite similar to previous 1968 R.632. It was new in 1968.') and fn 5 (lines 6997-6998: Oleynik v. Univ. of Calg. 2013 ABCA 395, 2013 CarswellAlta 2302 (one JA Nov 22) (¶'s 10-19), leave den 2014 ABCA 19, 2014 CarswellAlta 53. (Jan 16).; the same words as fn 2 of the 10.37 note, line 6906). Read against the official text: the rule text equals official 10.40 (EXACT_MATCH, no differences). (1) Related Provisions read against the official rules: '3.36 (failure to defend)' is a label for official 3.36 'Judgment in default of defence and noting in default'; '9.15(1) (b) (setting aside order on failure to appear)' is a paraphrase of 9.15(1)(b) (accident, mistake or insufficient notice); '10.16 (failure to appear on review)' is a label for official 10.16 'Absence of person at appointment for review' (the same list is printed under 10.16, see the 10.16 flag). (2) 'This was done and upheld, especially as deference is owed to the assessment officer's scheduling decisions' (fn 5, Oleynik v. Univ. of Calg.) has no antecedent: 'This' refers to a statement that is not printed in the note (the note has only this one sentence, printed directly after the Related Provisions), so the sentence cannot be read on its own; the rule itself says nothing about scheduling decisions or deference. (3) Oleynik v. Univ. of Calg. 2013 ABCA 395 is the case behind the 10.37 note fn 2 (large swathes of dates for the hearing) and is printed again at line 6997 (this rule) and, with paragraph 4, at line 7321; fn 5 has a stray full stop before the date ('CarswellAlta 53. (Jan 16).'), as in the 10.37 note. No supra or infra and no placeholder '(#_)' is used. The history footnote names an old rule (1968 R.632) and says the rule 'was new in 1968', not checked against any old-rule text; Book B has no commentary for this rule, so nothing in this note is corroborated by Book B.
